title: UK and EU Close to a Deal for Young Travellers
summary:
Young people in Britain and Europe could soon find it easier to live, work and travel in each other's countries. The UK and the European Union are expected to agree a new youth mobility scheme at a summit in Brussels on Friday.

The scheme would let the same number of young Britons into Europe as young Europeans into Britain. It aims to make it easier for young people to work and travel in both the EU and the UK. The UK already has similar schemes with 13 countries outside the EU, including Australia, Canada and India.

In 2024, the EU proposed letting 18- to 30-year-olds work or study in the EU and UK for up to four years. Labour, then in opposition, rejected the idea, arguing it amounted to bringing back freedom of movement. Since coming to government, the party has said it would consider a more restricted scheme, with a time limit, a cap on numbers and a ban on participants claiming benefits.

Two issues have been sticking points: the UK's request to limit numbers, and the EU's request that EU students pay the same tuition fees at UK universities as British students. Talks were "down to the wire" on Thursday, Downing Street said.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the deal could also bring lower food prices, lower costs for business and less red tape, plus a "Channel action plan" on immigration. A trade agreement could remove checks and paperwork for food companies exporting to the EU, which the government argues could add £5 billion to the economy. If a deal is secured, the government would introduce legislation to Parliament next week.

Not everyone is happy. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused Burnham of "reopening the divisions" of the Brexit referendum.
why_it_matters: If the deal goes ahead, young people will have more choices about where to work, study and travel — and the deal could also make food cheaper and business easier.

background_read: The UK left the European Union in a process called Brexit, and since then Britons and Europeans have not had an automatic right to live and work in each other's countries.
A youth mobility scheme is a deal that lets young adults spend a set time abroad to work, study or travel.
The UK already runs similar schemes with countries such as Australia and Canada.
Such deals are negotiated between governments, and any agreement still needs to be turned into law by Parliament.
